conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. I'll need to ask you a few questions to assess your situation.

First, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for:

**How old is your child?** This will help me determine which eligibility pathway applies to your situation:
- Under 16 years old
- Between 16 and 19 years old  
- 20 years or older

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Based on your situation profile, let me continue the assessment for Alex, who is 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Since Alex is 17 years old, I need to check their education or training status.

**Is Alex currently:**
1. In approved education or training?
2. Recently left education or training (within the last 20 weeks)?
3. Neither (not in education/training and didn't leave recently)?

This is important because children aged 16-19 can qualify for Child Benefit if they're in approved education or training, or in some cases for a short period after leaving education.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Based on your situation profile, Alex is 17 and in approved education. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check what type of education Alex is in. For 16-19 year olds, Child Benefit is only available for **approved (non-advanced) education**.

**What type of education or qualification is Alex studying?**

**Approved education includes:**
- A-levels, AS-levels
- T-levels
- Scottish Highers or Advanced Highers
- NVQ Level 1, 2, or 3
- BTEC Level 1, 2, or 3
- Access to Higher Education courses

**NOT approved (advanced education):**
- University degrees (Bachelor's, Master's, PhD)
- Higher National Certificate (HNC) or Diploma (HND)
- NVQ Level 4 or above
- Professional qualifications at Level 4+

Also, the education must be:
- **Full-time** (at least 12 hours per week of supervised study)
- **Not employer-funded** or part of an agreement for a future job with an employer

What type of course is Alex studying?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Let me continue with the assessment based on your situation profile. Alex is 17 and in approved education, so I'll navigate accordingly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, Alex is in approved education. Now I need to check their work situation.

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

This is important because children aged 16+ who work 24 hours or more per week are not eligible for Child Benefit, even if they're in education.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now I need to check if Alex is receiving any qualifying benefits in their own right.

**Is Alex NOT receiving any of the following benefits in their own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit
- Other income-related benefits

Children who receive these benefits in their own right are not eligible for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check if Alex is in an apprenticeship, as some types of apprenticeships disqualify from Child Benefit.

**Is Alex in any of the following types of apprenticeships?**
- Any type of apprenticeship in England (Intermediate, Advanced, Higher, or Degree Apprenticeships)
- Modern Apprenticeships in Scotland
- Apprenticeships in Wales (except Foundation level)

**Note:** Foundation Apprenticeships in Wales are approved and don't disqualify.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship. Now I need to check your residency status as the claimant.

**Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

You qualify if **ANY** of the following applies to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK**
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status AND are working (earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months)
4. You have pre-settled status AND are actively seeking work (up to 91 days)
5. You have pre-settled status AND have sufficient resources to support yourself and family (not claiming Income Support, income-based JSA, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit)
6. You have pre-settled status AND are studying with sufficient resources
7. You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with right to reside
8. You're a Crown servant living abroad or in certain qualifying countries

Do any of these apply to you?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! You meet the residency requirements. Now I need to check if you're responsible for Alex.

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

You're considered responsible if **ANY** of the following applies:

1. **You live with Alex**
2. You contribute to Alex's upkeep (paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit or equivalent in kind - including food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents)
3. You pay maintenance for Alex under a court order or agreement (amount equals or exceeds Child Benefit payment)

Which of these applies to your situation?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! You live with Alex, so you're considered responsible. Now I need to check if anyone else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

- No one else is claiming
- Someone else is claiming, but we've agreed that I should claim instead
- Someone else is claiming and there's a dispute about who should claim

Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at a time. If there's a dispute, HMRC will need to decide who has the greater responsibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! No one else is claiming for Alex. Now I need to check Alex's living situation.

**Where is Alex currently living?**

- In hospital
- In local authority care
- Fostered by someone else
- Living normally with you (or in normal accommodation)

This is important because there are special rules if a child is in hospital for extended periods, in care, or fostered.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Alex is living normally with you. One final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is the council providing financial support for Alex's living costs or accommodation? Generally, you cannot get Child Benefit if the local council is paying for the child.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Based on the information you've provided, **you ARE ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex!**

conversation.text:
## 🎉 You Are Eligible for Child Benefit!

**Summary:**
You meet all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Why you qualify:**
- ✅ Alex is 17 years old (within the 16-19 eligible age range)
- ✅ Alex is in approved (non-advanced) education
- ✅ Alex is not working 24+ hours per week
- ✅ Alex is not receiving benefits in their own right
- ✅ Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
- ✅ You meet UK residency requirements
- ✅ You're responsible for Alex (living together)
- ✅ No one else is claiming for Alex
- ✅ The local council is not paying for Alex's care

---

## Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware** of the High Income Child Benefit Charge if you or your partner earns over £60,000
5. **Payments will be made** every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

**Apply here:** https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

If you have any questions about the application process or need help, please don't hesitate to ask!
